newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Kohl announces North-South environment initiative.
newsitem.headline: Kohl announces North-South environment initiative.

text.p: Germany, Brazil, Singapore and South Africa launched a joint initiative on Monday aimed at overcoming North-South political differences hampering global environmental protection.

German Chancellor Helmut Kohl, speaking at the opening session of a U.N. conference taking stock of progress since the Rio Earth Summit in 1992, said the purpose of the initiative was to show that rich countries could take joint action with developing nations on vital environmental issues.

"By making this personal commitment we seek to lend the worldwide protection of the natural sources of life and the idea of sustainable development additional impetus and thus also to help make this special session of the (U.N.) General Assembly a success," Kohl said.

Kohl was due to give more details of the four-nation partnership at a news conference later on Monday with Brazilian President Fernando Henrique Cardoso, Deputy South African President Thabo Mbeki and Singaporean Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong.
Brazilian officials said the initiative would focus on measures aimed at protecting climate and forests as well as problems of urban development.
As part of the plan, Germany has agreed to host a conference in 2000 of the world's 21 largest cities to address the environmental strains caused by rapid urbanisation.

"We want to set an example of how countries in differing stages of development can demonstrate, through creativity and concerted action, the political will to render Agenda 21 a concrete reality," Cardoso said in his speech to the assembly.

Agenda 21 was the blueprint for sustainable development adopted at the Rio summit, which was dogged by the sort of North-South differences -- especially over finance -- that Monday's partnership hopes to overcome.
